news.title: A transparent pricing model for AI
news.gist: Pass-through pricing, where customers pay for model tokens at or near list price plus a platform fee, is spreading, but Poyar argues it suits only products whose value can’t be separated from token use; the rest should charge for what sets them apart.
points: Clay split its pricing into data passed through near cost and higher-margin platform actions, which Poyar likens to Costco’s membership model
Gumloop shows a cost breakdown on every chat so customers can switch to a cheaper model, and built a tool that forecasts credit use
The risks: looking like a wrapper around someone else’s model, and revenue that rises and falls with other companies’ price decisions
Anthropic’s linked billing beta lets platforms such as Asana, Linear and Ramp bill end customers for Claude API use without sharing keys
nums: drop in price per token since January 2025, per OpenRouter data
OpenRouter’s take rate on its Standard plan, rising on Business
Gumloop’s orchestration fee on top of tokens and compute billed at cost
drop in Gumloop’s price per credit
rise in Gumloop’s Pro trial conversion rate
news.why: When a vendor offers AI at cost plus a fee, add the fee and any platform charge to your expected token spend and compare that with a bundled plan, since falling model prices only reach you if the pass-through is real.

news.title: Shopify introduced a tax calculation fee
news.gist: Shopify added a percentage fee for tax calculated through Tax managed by Shopify, and PricingSaaS reads it as a usage-style charge stacked on top of plan prices rather than a change to any tier’s price.
points: The listed rates apply after an introductory discount period, so merchants may be paying less today
The page doesn’t say what the percentage is applied to, or whether it stacks on payment-processing fees
A Self-managed tax mode option appeared in the same feature table
It is the first pricing-restructure change Pulse has recorded for Shopify, which usually changes pricing slowly

news.why: Merchants using Shopify’s tax engine should work out the fee against their own sales and check when the introductory discount ends before budgeting for next year.

news.title: Mistral removed Pro’s bundled API credits
news.gist: Mistral stopped listing a monthly API credit perk on its Pro plan and opened model-training opt-out to Free, Pro and Team, which PricingSaaS reads as tightening its usage economics while removing a governance objection.
points: Pro’s other listed features, such as faster responses and image generation, are unchanged
Training opt-out used to be listed only for Enterprise, so it no longer needs a sales conversation
It follows an October cut to Free plan API credits, a short gap by Mistral’s usual pace
Most credit changes Pulse sees reprice credits rather than remove them, so a straight cut is the rarer move

news.why: Teams that ran API calls against Pro’s included credits should budget for that usage separately now, since nothing on the page replaces the allowance.

news.title: Mintlify tested a paid $150 Starter plan
news.gist: Mintlify showed some visitors a new paid Starter tier with editor seats and a capped AI-credit allowance, a day after renaming its free Starter plan to Free, and PricingSaaS reads it as a live A/B test.
points: The test arm was tied to a variant cookie, and the control version showed no Starter price
Pro’s card now calls out password protection and advanced analytics to stand apart from the cheaper tier
The Agent and Autopilot AI features sit in the new tier, so they become paid features rather than free extras
Existing free users keep their plan under the Free name, with price and editor limit unchanged

news.why: If Mintlify’s page shows you a Starter price, get it confirmed in writing, since most visitors don’t see the plan yet and its credit cap may push a team to Pro sooner than the seat count suggests.

news.title: Krea cut Basic plan’s Seedance video allowance despite a model upgrade
news.gist: Krea’s Basic plan now gets about half as many Seedance videos a month after the model moved up a version, and PricingSaaS argues that pairing an upgrade with a quota cut hides a higher cost per video.

The cut landed four days after Krea’s Black Friday discounts
Pulse’s diff shows the cut on Basic only, not on Pro, Max or Business
The author suggests holding quotas steady on a model upgrade and announcing any cut on its own

news.title: Developer Tool Pricing Changes: November 16–22, 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals’ digest for our week is mostly model retirements at Cloudflare, Azure, xAI and MiniMax, plus Lemon Squeezy closing to new stores; Crowdin’s plan rework and Mistral’s dropped API credits are the only direct price moves.
points: Requests to retired Workers AI and Azure OpenAI models fail with HTTP 410 Gone rather than moving to another model
Azure’s retirements include o1, o3 and o4-mini, and Microsoft Foundry also retires a Llama 4 model with no replacement named
Lemon Squeezy stops processing transactions, renewals included, at the end of March 2027 and points stores to Stripe Managed Payments
NVIDIA retired more free NIM endpoints, including gpt-oss-20b and a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash endpoint
nums: Workers AI models removed on 20 Nov

hosted words on Crowdin’s Free plan, down from 60,000

news.why: If your code calls any of the retired models, requests now fail outright, so check model names and price the named replacements before your next bill.

news.title: The B2B buyer journey with AI
news.gist: An analysis of real prompts about buying SaaS and AI tools finds buyers use AI mostly in the middle of the funnel to compare and test a shortlist, and that pricing is the top commercial theme, showing up early for AI products.
points: Discovery of a new category still happens outside AI, so vendors need demand from other channels
Many buyers ask AI to rank options, so position on the list matters, not just being mentioned
Opaque pricing is a risk from the first prompt, and few B2B companies have made their pricing readable for AI
Recommended products then get tested with follow-up questions about capability and cost
nums: real user prompts about buying SaaS and AI products that were analyzed
share of prompts in the middle of the funnel
share of commercial prompts focused on pricing
share of top-of-funnel queries about pricing for AI coding agents and website builders, against 2% for CRM and ERP
news.why: AI assistants now summarize vendor pricing for buyers, so check what an assistant says a tool costs against the live pricing page before you shortlist it.

patterns.t: Free plans get a hard number
patterns.p: Several vendors put a cap on free plans that had none, or cut the free allowance outright; at ClickUp the AI trial went first. A free plan that fits today can stop fitting without a price change. Three of these records come from PricingSaaS reports.

patterns.t: New meters on things the plan used to cover
patterns.p: Vendors put new meters on work the plan used to cover: tax calculation at Shopify, agent hours at Warp, traces and pipelines at Buildkite and Pulumi. Each fee looks small, but it grows with use and can end up costing more than the seat or plan price.

stats_analysis.t: Changes that cost buyers more led clearly
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that cost buyers more vs less; the other 34 repackaged plans
stats_analysis.p: Increases ran well ahead of cuts, from Hugging Face’s Enterprise seat and Jobber’s AI Receptionist add-on to smaller free plans at Notion and ClickUp. On the buyer’s side most gains were looser limits, with outright price cuts at Archbee, Vercel and DeepSeek. More than half of this week’s records come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Larger companies split, but their free plans shrank
stats_analysis.figNote: changes at tier 1 and 2 companies that cost buyers more
stats_analysis.p: Three of the four were free-plan cuts, at Notion, ClickUp and Scribe, and the fourth was Shopify’s new tax fee. Buyers gained from Zoho’s free plan in LATAM, Wispr Flow’s unlimited free meetings and Cognition dropping its per-seat fee in what looks like a test. Shopify’s record is a PricingSaaS report; the rest are our own captures.

stats_analysis.t: Limits tightened exactly as often as they loosened
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that tightened vs loosened a plan limit
stats_analysis.p: A steady list price says little about which way a plan moved this week. Tightening hit credits and caps at GitLab, Nifty, Nereo and Krea; loosening raised seat, website and MCP caps at LiveAgent, Browse AI and Moqups. Many of these records are PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: AI was in about a third of the changes
stats_analysis.figNote: changes involving AI features, models or credits
stats_analysis.p: Many AI changes resized credit allowances rather than list prices, in both directions. AI also moved between tiers: ClickUp took it off Free and Bearly AI put Deep Research behind a higher plan, while Dinero and Tango added AI features to their free plans.

Free plans lost room at Notion, ClickUp, Scribe and Salesmotion, and Spoki dropped its free plan altogether. Zoho added a free Zoho One plan in LATAM, and Wispr Flow, Benchmark Email and Sapling widened theirs. Spoki, Sapling and several smaller cases are PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.figNote: promotion records this week, against 128 pricing changes
stats_analysis.p: Promotions ran at about two thirds the count of real pricing changes, led by first-year discounts on annual plans and model-usage discounts at AI tools such as ElevenLabs and Krea. Promo prices end, so check the renewal price before signing for a year; some promotion records come from PricingSaaS reports.

news_trends.t: Credit allowances are the lever vendors keep pulling
news_trends.p: PricingSaaS’s 180-day count of credit and usage-billing changes has risen with nearly every article that cites it (definitions vary slightly). This week Mistral dropped Pro’s API credits and Krea cut a video quota, while our captures saw GitLab shrink included credits and Klaviyo double its AI allowance.

news_trends.t: AI sold closer to cost, with the margin in a fee
news_trends.p: Across two months the stories describe vendors billing model usage at or near cost and earning on something else: Gumloop’s orchestration fee, Linear’s seat, the labs’ subscriptions with bundled API credits. This week Growth Unhinged set out when that works, and Warp added a per-agent-hour platform fee.

news_trends.t: Model retirements keep moving traffic onto new rates
news_trends.p: AgentDeals’ digests have logged model and endpoint retirements almost every week since October, and this week Cloudflare and Azure retired models outright, with no fallback. Hugging Face delisting its H100 endpoints and Krea cutting a quota on a model upgrade show that a model change can quietly change what you pay for.
